Ismail And 3 Ors

on 13 October, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.646 of 2023
Judgment:

Aggrieved by the impugned order dated 01.12.2011 on the file of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- V Additional District Judge, Vijayawada, passed in M.V.O.P.No.238 of 2007, whereby the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim against the respondents 1 and 2, the instant appeal is preferred by the appellant-Respondent No.2- Insurance Company.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claimants filed a Claim Petition under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the respondents praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- towards compensation on account of death of deceased Nallamothu Suvarthamma in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 09.09.2005.

4. Facts germane to dispose of this appeal may be briefly stated as follows:
On 09.09.2005 at about 5.15 p.m. Smt Nallamothu Suvarthamma, hereinafter referred to as 'deceased', and her colleagues boarded the auto bearing No.AP16 TV 2180, hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle', at Kottagattu center, VTPS,
Kondapalli to go to their respective houses in Shakthi Nagar, Ibrahimpatnam, after the duty in VTPS, and when the auto reached near State Bank of Hyderabad, the driver of the auto drove the same in a rash and negligent manner without following the traffic rules and to avoid the accident, suddenly turned the vehicle on the left side and crossed the road, due to which the deceased fell down from the auto and sustained multiple injuries, later succumbed to injuries while undergoing treatment.
The deceased was working as a contract labour under one J.T.Tataji and earning Rs.2,300/- per month and she was hale and healthy by the date of accident.

5. The respondents 1 and 2 filed counters separately denying the claim of the claimants and contended that the claimants are not entitled any compensation and the respondents 1 and 2 are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i. Whether the deceased N.Suvarthamma died in a motor vehicle accident occurred United India Insurance Company Limited vs Sri Nallamothu Ismail And 3 Ors on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66926234/
1 on 09.09.2005 due to rash and negligent driving of crime vehicle auto bearing No.AP16TV 2180 by the driver of R1?

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited vs Sri Nallamothu Ismail And 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ii. What is the correct age and income of the deceased by the time of accident?
iii. Whether the petitioners are entitled to the compensation as prayed for?

If so, from whom and to what amount?
iv.
Whether there is any contributory negligence of the deceased at the time of accident apart from the negligence of the driver of R1?

v. To what relief?
7.

During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioners,
PW1 to PW3 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A8 were marked.
On behalf of respondents RW1 and RW2 were examined and Ex.B1 to Ex.B3 were marked.

8. At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same, the Tribunal has given a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.2,82,600/- to the claimant Nos.1 and 3 towards compensation.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the second respondent Insurance Company filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.
9. Heard Smt A.Jayanthi, learned counsel for second respondent Insurance Company.
Inspite of service of notice, there is no representation on behalf of petitioners/claimants.

10. Now, the point for consideration is:
 Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any  interference?
If so, to what extent?

11. POINT :
In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle,
the petitioners relied on the evidence of PW1 to PW3.

The evidence on record clearly goes to show that First Information Report was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle and charge sheet was also laid against the said driver of the offending vehicle for driving the offending auto in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the deceased sat beside the driver of the offending vehicle, due to imbalance, she fell down and sustained injuries and there was a contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.

As seen from the material on record, it clearly reveals that the deceased sat beside the driver of the offending vehicle, but the material on record also clearly reveals that the driver of the offending auto drove the auto in a rash and negligent manner without following rules, due to his rash and negligent driving, suddenly the auto was turned turtle on the left side and due to which the deceased fell down from the auto and sustained injuries on her head.

The facts remain is that by the time of accident, the deceased sat beside the driver of the offending vehicle, which is not permissible under law, therefore, there was a contributory negligence of 25% on the part of the deceased in causing the accident.

On considering the entire material on record, I am of the considered view that there was a negligence of 75% on the part of the driver of the offending auto bearing No.AP16TV 2180 and so also there is a 25% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
13.
The contention of the claimants is that the deceased was an employee in VTPS and used to earn Rs.2,300/- per month.

On considering the entire material on record, the Tribunal arrived the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.2,300/-, i.e.,
Rs,27,600/- per annum.

As the dependents on the deceased are three in number,
1/3rd income of the deceased has been deducted by the Tribunal towards personal expenses of the deceased.
After deducting 1/3rd amount, the net income available to the dependents on the deceased was Rs.18,400/- (27,600 - 9,200) per annum.
The age of the deceased is 29 years by the date of accident.
On considering the material on record, the Tribunal rightly applied the multiplier of 14.
Accordingly, an amount of Rs.2,57,600/- (18,400 x 14) is awarded to the petitioner Nos.1 and 3 towards loss of dependency.

In addition to the above amount, the Tribunal also awarded an amount of Rs.5,000/- towards loss of consortium, an amount of Rs.5,000/- towards transportation, an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards love and affection and an amount of Rs.5,000/- towards funeral expenses of the deceased.

In total,
the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.2,82,600/- to the petitioners towards compensation.
It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle is insured with the second respondent Insurance Company and the policy is in force.
The learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the driver of the offending vehicle is not having valid driving licence to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

The Tribunal by assailing cogent reasons clearly held that the second respondent Insurance Company failed to prove that the driver of the offending vehicle is not having any valid and effective driving licence by the time of accident.

As seen from the material on record, charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle and no charge was framed against the driver of the auto under violations of terms and conditions of Motor Vehicles Act.

The Tribunal by assailing cogent reasons, came to conclusion that in the absence of any evidence this court safely came to conclusion that as on the date of accident, the driver of offending vehicle is having valid driving licence.

Therefore, for the foregoing reasons, the Tribunal rightly fixed the liability on both United India Insurance Company Limited vs Sri Nallamothu Ismail And 3 Ors on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66926234/
3 the respondents and directed the second respondent Insurance Company to deposit the said amount.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For the reasons stated above 25% of the compensation amount has to be deducted towards 25% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
If 25% of the compensation amount is deducted from out of Rs.2,82,600/-, it comes to Rs.2,11,950/- (2,82,600 - 70,650).
Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled an amount of Rs.2,11,950/- towards total compensation.

14. In the result, this appeal is partly allowed and the order dated 01.12.2011 passed in MVOP No.238 of 2007 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- V Additional District Judge,
Vijayawada is modified by reducing the compensation amount from Rs.2,82,600/- to Rs.2,11,950/-.
